fields.features_heading: What Payroll Needs Before the First Deduction
fields.features_subheading: A signed sheet in a drawer leaves payroll guessing. Build a form that records the amount, the schedule and who signed.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the deduction type

The employee picks a pay advance, a uniform, a tool kit or parking, and the form asks only what that type needs. An advance asks for the total; parking asks for a start date.
fields.feature_2:
Every paycheck listed before signing

Enter the total and the amount per paycheck, and the form lists each deduction with its pay date. The employee reads the full schedule on the same screen where they sign.
fields.feature_3:
A signature from any phone

Employees sign with a finger on a phone or with a mouse at a desk. The app saves the signature next to the authorization text they saw, so payroll can pull up both later.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that say a form is in, nothing more

Payroll gets an email or a Slack message that an authorization or a stop request has arrived, with a link. Amounts and names stay in the app instead of sitting in an inbox.
fields.feature_5:
Balances that count down each payday

Every active authorization shows what it takes each payday and the balance owed. When one paycheck's worth remains, the app marks the deduction final so payroll can end it.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the form beside your payroll system. Every signed authorization stays in a database that you own.

fields.usecase_heading: One Form for Every Deduction Staff Agree To
fields.tab_content_1:
Every $50 deduction listed before he signs

Jonah Whitcombe needed a $600 pay advance from Delmont Freight. He picks the advance on the form, and it lays out 12 deductions of $50, each with its payday. He reads the list, then signs. Payroll gets an email that says an authorization is in, with a link and no amounts.
fields.tab_content_2:
Her signature goes in before the kit order does

Marisol Avery orders a $240 tool kit through Kestrel Mechanical's form on her phone, between two service calls. She picks 4 paychecks of $60. The submit button stays locked until she signs with her finger, and her signature is saved next to the exact wording she agreed to.
fields.tab_content_3:
In by Wednesday noon, off Friday's paycheck

Tess Lindqvist pays $25 a paycheck to park at Brookline Grocers. After a move across town, she files a stop request on Tuesday. Any request in by Wednesday noon comes off that Friday's paycheck, and Friday is the first payday without her deduction. Payroll gets a Slack message that a stop request is in.
fields.tab_content_4:
With $45 left, this payday ends it

Halvorsen Dental's office manager keeps four deductions open on one screen, each with its amount per paycheck and the balance left. Marcus Hale bought dental loupes at $45 a paycheck, and $45 is all that remains. The app marks his deduction final. This payday is his last one.

faq_heading: Payroll Deduction Authorization Form Template FAQ

plan.angle: The top 10 is blank paper: Word and PDF downloads, a university and a state agency PDF, an HR association sample, and a six-template pack (loan, uniform, one-time). Each is a box for an amount and a signature line. This page is for the payroll or HR lead who builds the authorization as a working form: the employee picks the deduction type, sees the per-paycheck amount and the number of paychecks before signing, signs on a phone, can ask to stop a deduction, and payroll sees every active authorization and its remaining balance in a database the employer owns. Alerts carry no pay details, only that a form is in and a link.
tab_stories: At Delmont Freight, dock worker Jonah Whitcombe takes a $600 pay advance; the form shows 12 deductions of $50 before he signs, and payroll gets an email that says only that an authorization is in, with a link.
